claims: President Trump fired Attorney General Pam Bondi in April 2026.
Attorney General Pam Bondi's tenure was 14 months.
Pam Bondi was replaced on an acting basis by Todd Blanche.
President Trump was frustrated over Pam Bondi's failure to aggressively prosecute his political enemies.
President Trump was frustrated over Pam Bondi's "limited success" in acting on his grievances.
President Trump was dissatisfied with Pam Bondi's performance.
President Trump was dissatisfied with the pace of investigations.
President Trump was dissatisfied with Pam Bondi's handling of Epstein-related files.
President Trump was annoyed by Pam Bondi's inability to secure indictments against perceived enemies, including cases involving former FBI Director James Comey and NY Attorney General Letitia James.
President Trump felt Pam Bondi failed to fully "execute on his vision".
President Trump felt Pam Bondi failed to manage the Justice Department as a tool for retribution.
President Trump wanted a more aggressive approach.
President Trump considered replacing Pam Bondi with more combative, trusted allies.
